assumptions: Target competitor has a public product footprint with established pricing tiers.
The bound workspace contains documentation or codebase defining core features and architecture.
Outputs must enforce radical technical honesty by disclosing at least two competitor strengths.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex procedure session using standard isolated and fenced execution.
Processing time scales with project documentation depth, taking between 60 to 180 seconds.
Zero paid third-party API keys or external data extraction services required.
effects: Writes reports/MIGRATION_BATTLECARD.md in the project state.
Zero external mutations, webhook transmissions, or credential persistence.

cases.description: Standard developer tool displacement with medium complexity (PostHog vs Mixpanel).

inputs.target_persona: Growth Engineers, Product Managers, and CTOs
inputs.core_differentiators: Self-hosted or EU cloud, open source, unlimited event retention, SQL access via ClickHouse, 70% lower TCO.
inputs.known_limitations: Mixpanel has more polished out-of-the-box non-technical funnel visualizations and older mobile SDK maturity.

cases.description: High-complexity infrastructure migration requiring dual-write shadow ingestion (OpenTelemetry vs Datadog).

inputs.target_persona: DevOps Leads and VP of Infrastructure
inputs.core_differentiators: OpenTelemetry native, predictable host-based billing with no custom metrics overage penalty.
inputs.known_limitations: Datadog has 600+ turnkey vendor integrations and enterprise FedRAMP High certification.

cases.description: Low-complexity stateless API migration with drop-in SDK replacement (Resend vs SendGrid).

inputs.core_differentiators: Modern React Email support, sub-second API latency, no shared IP reputation penalty, transparent pricing.
inputs.known_limitations: SendGrid has higher legacy transactional volume capacity and established enterprise marketing automation suites.

rubric.question: Does the report explicitly disclose at least two areas where the incumbent vendor holds a legitimate structural advantage?
Is the report completely free of unsubstantiated marketing superlatives like revolutionary or game-changer, relying instead on concrete technical specifications?
Does the migration plan provide a concrete 4-stage pipeline including dual-write shadow ingestion and delta reconciliation before traffic cutover?
Are the switching payback timeline and engineering migration investment calculated with concrete dollar amounts and breakeven horizons?
